item.title: AI Stocks Daily — Nov 27, 2026
item.description: AI bubble: Peruvian Bull: a surprising amount of the AI boom was borrowed in Japan - OpenAI has signed long-term chip/compute deals it cannot cover from earnings (FT: ~$856B of compute/data-center spending through 2030 vs ~$36B revenue this year, ~$278B more burn than intake), and SoftBank has put ~$65B into OpenAI, even selling its entire Nvidia stake last year to help fund the bet; AI bubble: The Tech Report / Ed Zitron: the circular-deals critique is mainstreaming - Bloomberg's framing that Nvidia could end up like Lucent and Nortel, whose telecom customers ran aground and turned vendor loans into bad debt that destroyed the suppliers' balance sheets, and the shift from 'Nvidia supports its partners' to 'is Nvidia just feeding money to itself?'; AI bubble: Peruvian Bull: the banks behind the buildout are trying to hand off the risk - MUFG and JPMorgan led a record $38B loan for OpenAI sites in Texas and Wisconsin and took over six months to pass most of it to other lenders, ING is trying to sell data-center loans, Barclays has looked to buy insurance against AI borrower defaults, and a BoJ hike expected Dec 17-18 would raise SoftBank's borrowing cost further (3.9% a year ago to 4.75% in September); AI bubble: FinVid / CNBC panel (counterweight): to run away from Nvidia here you have to believe the AI trade is over, the infrastructure buildout is done and the company will never grow again - the market is becoming deaf to the Huang headlines, guidance was raised on the last call, and holders plan to add if volatility moves the stock their way; AI supply/demand: FinVid: demand is not the problem, supply is - the world stays compute-constrained at least through calendar 2028, frontier labs' revenues are directly tied to compute (more compute would mean more revenue), agentic adoption is only in its early stages, and physical AI is the next demand surge, which Nvidia's CFO has called a multi-trillion-dollar opportunity; AI supply/demand: Parkev Tatevosian: Wall Street EPS-growth forecasts are at record levels even as AI stocks crash - Broadcom ~55%/yr and Nvidia ~49%/yr - fuelled by data-center demand, with the five big US hyperscalers (Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft, Oracle, Meta) set to have spent over $900B on capex by the end of 2026, most of it building data centers; AI supply/demand: The Tech Report / Ed Zitron: Oracle claims it will be free-cash-flow positive in H2 FY28 and print $30B+ in FY29 (which he does not believe), and a TD Cowen channel check found evidence Nvidia was renting data-center capacity and sub-leasing it to Oracle to keep it off the balance sheet - the vendor-financing question in the AI buildout; AI supply/demand: Stas Talks Stocks (per Bloomberg): Blackwell chips were discovered at a Shanghai data center - a GB300 NVL72 rack and a GB200 server that were never permitted for export to China without a US license; Bloomberg traced the GB300 rack's serial number to its Taiwan manufacturer, Gigabyte Technology, and how the hardware reached China remains unknown - a 3,300lb, two-metre rack of the size Jensen Huang had argued was too difficult to smuggle; Watchlist: The Hostile Takeover: Friday's half-session leadership split - Micron held at $642 (+6.7%), Marvell $137 (+4.8%, reports Tuesday), AMD $418 (+2.9%), but Nvidia gapped to $152, fell to $145 and sat ~$149 at noon (-0.2% vs Wednesday); the thinnest session of the year gives no verdict by itself; Watchlist: Parkev Tatevosian: Nvidia's return on invested capital is 105% - unsustainable, but even at 40% it would be over twice its cost of capital; Broadcom's ROIC is 26% and could rise toward 40% as it capitalizes on tens of billions in backlog orders to build proprietary chips for Alphabet and OpenAI; both trade at their cheapest valuations in years with record profits and margins; Watchlist: Moneyvest: after the sell-off the forward multiples are stark - Nvidia ~9x next year's earnings, Broadcom 15.5x, Marvell just under 18x, with Micron and SanDisk under 13x trailing and Applied Materials ~30x; versus their 50-day averages the semis are down hard - Intel -37%, SMCI -31%, Lam Research -29%, Nvidia -26%, AMAT and AMD ~-25%; Watchlist: Moneyvest: the sell-off prices in an earnings decline - but even if next year's estimates for Nvidia, Broadcom, AMD, ASML, TSMC and Marvell were cut in half and the multiples doubled, they still would not look bad; he concludes this is a massive overreaction in semiconductors, of a kind seen in 2022 and 2024; Watchlist: Moneyvest: the ecosystem is interdependent - TSMC cannot survive without ASML, Nvidia cannot survive without TSMC, Lam Research or Marvell - and the technical levels to watch are Nvidia support ~$130, AMD validating ~$362, Broadcom validating $280 support, with ASML 'the bones behind the entire operation' and on his radar after its fall; Watchlist: The Hostile Takeover: the bottoming checklist - QQQ holding Wednesday's 634 close on a down day, NYSE/Nasdaq new lows shrinking, and Nvidia stopping its lower highs; invalidation is a close below QQQ 608, SMH 394 or Micron 548; Monday Nov 30 is month-end, so pension/60-40 rebalancing buying will fight tax-loss selling and the real confirmation window is Tuesday to Thursday

item.title: AI Stocks Daily — Nov 26, 2026
item.description: AI bubble: tastylive / Mark Thornton (Mises Institute): the 'skyscraper curse' fits AI data centers - huge, expensive, technology-dense real-estate builds that only appear at a cycle peak; data centers are the modern flat skyscraper; tastylive / Thornton: the mismatch - chips with a ~3-year shelf life financed with long-maturity debt, companies stretching inferior chips because they have no alternative; asked where the vulnerability sits (tech firms, financiers, or the banking system), he says all of the above; tastylive / Thornton: the financing fiasco - cash-rich tech firms now adding $300-500B of debt a year, with private credit, private equity and insurance/annuity exposure on top, and Jensen Huang as 'bagman' pushing liquidity to suppliers and customers; the pattern is not unprecedented - canals, railroads, electrification and the late-90s bubble all ran hype, then reset, then the long real story; FinVid / CNBC-Bloomberg panel: S&P has just put Nvidia on negative credit watch - not a downgrade, but watching for a potential cut - as the panel debates where liability sits if the Huang storm turns, with Nvidia versus Jensen as separate risks. Supply/demand: FinVid: TrendForce - DRAM stays under-supplied and tight through 2027 even as Chinese CSPs trim orders (2027 DRAM revenue forecast cut to ~$1.15T, still +69% YoY); North American CSPs instantly absorbed the freed supply; Taiwanese ODMs report B300 lead times of 26-40 weeks and GB300 at 14-26 weeks, demand far outpacing supply - so the fall in GPU rental prices looks like the Commerce rule change / Southeast Asia disruption, not weakening demand; FinVid: the world is compute-constrained through at least calendar 2028 - no GPUs sitting dark like dot-com fiber, hyperscalers building into signed contracts and prepayments and monetizing capacity instantly; agentic AI drove an inference-demand inflection, frontier labs' revenues are surging, and if they had more compute they would have more revenue - demand is not the problem, supply is; Finance Deep Dive / Cramer: how much of Nvidia's investment wave was to preserve AI - and how much to stop AMD and Broadcom? Giving money to neoclouds that might not otherwise get financing locks them into the Nvidia world and shuts out competitors, just as real competition arrives for the first time; Cramer concludes Nvidia wins and its hegemony is still intact. Watchlist: FinVid / Dan Ives (via CNBC): Huang drew a hard line against traditional succession planning at the all-hands; Ives raised his Nvidia price target to $250 on Jensen's return - the one executive who can run the ecosystem at this cycle's pace - and sees the December congressional appearances as the path from $250 to $300; Finance Deep Dive / Cramer: AMD finally has a competitive chip but its chips are expensive, and Cramer is focused on Nvidia's Rubin and then Feynman; the loyalty-card analogy - Nvidia funding locks customers in so the card only works in its store - and his conclusion that even with less China selling and more competition, Nvidia wins and its hegemony is intact; Stas Talks Stocks: if the SEC probe clears, Nvidia could push back toward $200 in Q1/Q2 - but into year-end most AI names face tax-loss harvesting, with the memory / picks-and-shovels names down ~50% sold into every pop, setting up potential buy-backs in the new year if fundamentals hold; Ricky Gutierrez: most people trying to trade or invest in Nvidia got shaken out - overexposed and overleveraged - even though it has been one of the greatest long-term investments; both can be true, it has seen multiple 50% drawdowns, and position sizing is what lets an investor survive the volatility.

item.title: AI Stocks Daily — Nov 25, 2026
item.description: dummy finance: Fed governor Michelle Bowman estimated roughly a quarter of the excess inflation above target came directly from the AI build-out - the Fed's leadership now views AI spending itself as an inflation source it may have to lean against; dummy finance: the Fed is designed to protect the financial system, not stock prices - it lent to banks in March 2023 and raised rates anyway, and the 11 aggressive cuts of 2001 did not stop the Nasdaq's fall; Prof G / George Noble: the 'Bank of Nvidia' is effectively in receivership under government supervision, so the speed of Nvidia's vendor-financing liquidity to loss-making customers will slow - less money from Nvidia, Anthropic and OpenAI, and 'the whole thing is going to explode'; Eli the Computer Guy: TSMC is reportedly setting balance-sheet-based credit limits for AI customers, demanding extra cash above the limit and prepayment from some ASIC clients to reserve capacity - watch what they do, not what they say; MonkeyExplains: the 2008 parallel - hundreds of billions of AI debt mentioned only in footnotes, sold to the same kinds of investors, resting on one assumption, that AI demand only goes up; if the line stops going up, it could make 2008 look small; Eli the Computer Guy: prepayment is friction - cash prepaid to TSMC cannot go to marketing, sales, or building the data centers the GPUs go into, so credit limits take money off the AI buildout table; The Tech Verdict: OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar warns internally she worries OpenAI might not be able to pay for its future computing contracts - while OpenAI slashes inference prices (GPT-5.6 Luna cut 80% to $0.20 per million tokens three weeks after launch), needing fewer buildings for every answer it gives; The Tech Verdict: OpenAI's first custom chip, built with Broadcom from a blank slate, went design-to-tape-out in nine months for deployment by end-2026 - every custom chip is a slice of Nvidia's margin OpenAI doesn't pay; one estimate puts OpenAI's Q1 2026 adjusted gross margin at ~33% vs its 46% target; FinVid / CNBC-Fox panel: every hyperscaler said it was supply-constrained on its last earnings call, and the clouds are building into contracted demand with signed contracts and prepayments - fundamentally different from the dot-com bubble's build-it-and-hope; Brian Stoffel's derail-risk list: circular financing leaves Nvidia on the hook if it doesn't work out, the AI trade is a narrow slice carrying the economy, capex growth rates have already started to fall, depreciation will make spenders' costs look bigger - and the fifth risk, compute prices falling fast, is the one that could really derail everything (older Nvidia chip prices are higher for now); FinVid / CNBC-Fox panel: Nvidia needs a real succession plan so Jensen's eventual departure doesn't trigger another leadership vacuum and stock slide - then Micron: management sees memory and storage supply-demand tighter in 2027 and 2028 than in 2026, contracted into at least 2H 2028; Motley Fool: stock one is Intel (INTC) as a different way to benefit from Jensen's return - recent earnings showed an extremely weak consumer CPU market as PC pricing stays expensive; Motley Fool: the equipment pick (AMAT) - advanced packaging is expected to grow north of 90% next year and is one of the cycle's biggest constraints; Nvidia and TSMC both flag CoWoS, and Intel sees packaging as one of its biggest growth opportunities; Dividend Talks works through his 10-stock DCF ranking: base cases imply large margins of safety, but the models hinge on the next round of factory spending arriving on time - and the Broadcom case shows the fragility, with ~72% of its DCF value sitting after year 10 at a 9% discount rate; Brian Stoffel: SK Hynix and Micron went from ~$1B to ~$60B of free cash flow, and their FCF margins are extraordinarily high versus their 10-year medians (AMD too) - while Broadcom's and Nvidia's sit only modestly above median, even as S&P cash profits run 27% below stated profits, a gap last seen in the late-90s build-out; Finance Deep Dive / Cramer close: the backlash runs both ways - national security brushed aside on one side, ethics ignored on the other; the board's four days wasn't enough to investigate, the China chip story was more complicated than it looked, and Cramer changed his mind when the facts changed

item.title: AI Stocks Daily — Nov 24, 2026
item.description: AI bubble: Stoic Finance: if the bubble pops the trillions poured into data centers and the jobs vanish with the index gains - a severe recession follows; Huang's saga only made that a few percent more likely, and Trump pressured the board to keep the bubble moving; Economist who called 2008 (via Owen Jones): market value is now more than twice GDP vs ~1.5x at the tech-bubble peak; a 30-50% fall cuts consumption ~2% of GDP, data-center construction falls with it, and the debt sits opaquely in private credit - 'we find out who's swimming naked'; Breaking Points: Huang's return doesn't solve the underlying problems - AI developers are finding it harder to raise debt and equity, neoclouds and the Anthropic IPO stay weak, and regulation is coming one way or the other. Supply/demand: Eli the Computer Guy: the oversupply evidence - dark GPUs, Amazon GPUs going straight to warehouses, ~600,000 GPUs sitting in Hong Kong, a TSMC surplus, and Colette Kress moving to shut the China gray channels that carry ~20% of actual lit-up sales; Bloomberg / MUFG: the pullback widens spreads and changes data-center financing pricing structurally, but GPU-financing demand is not going away - a secular, transformational trend with volatility and differentiation, not a cyclical event; Yahoo Finance panel: GPU and rental pricing keep rising while token pricing falls - an unsustainable model; some Nvidia margin pressure would actually help adoption and share, and the bulls' supercycle claim (Micron's president sees no stabilization point) meets the cycle skeptics; Yahoo Finance panel: one unnamed neocloud just had a massive contract canceled - trace the ripple through the whole supply chain when financing tightens; counterweight on Anthropic: the IPO was exceptionally successful, upsized into a bad macro backdrop, still above issue. Watchlist: Parkev Tatevosian: Nvidia at these prices and prospects is a great long-term deal, then into beaten-down Micron - now ~$700 after trading at $1,255; Parkev Tatevosian on TSMC: the best manufacturing company in the world, $356 after a $487 high against his $505 fair value - the primary manufacturer for Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom and Apple, so good that even Intel outsources to it; then ASML, the supplier to all of them; Tyler Hill on why AMD is making a lower low: the ~337M-share resale registration (~20.5% of shares out) is not AMD selling stock - it is mostly OpenAI and Meta warrants, up to 160M shares each, that vest only as they buy Instinct GPUs; CNBC / Jim Cramer defends Nvidia on circular financing: the bears say the deals sour, clients default and Nvidia drags the Nasdaq down, but the government is unlikely to stop them - and at 10x next year's earnings on ~75% sales growth the stock deserves 12x, about $199; Parkev Tatevosian: with backlog significant and shortages throughout the supply chain, Huang's return mitigates the disruption - two decades of trust with TSMC, the hyperscalers and the server makers that a new team could not replicate; Investing Tutorial: the bull case needs reassuring updates on supply, execution, margins and demand plus reduced regulatory uncertainty - set against the bear warning that Monday's rally may have been short covering, not lasting demand.

Watchlist: FinVid/King Lip - Nvidia's brain-drain risk as AMD and Broadcom call its engineers, the AI capex cycle is a durable multi-year engine not a bubble, and Anthropic's IPO is over six times oversubscribed; FinVid - the bull case: the world is compute-constrained through 2028, no GPUs sit dark, agentic AI is inflecting inference demand, and physical AI is Nvidia's next multi-trillion leg; Mohsin Ali - Nvidia fell 32% in five and a half weeks, $1.7T of market value gone, and the full timeline from the spy reports to Huang's Nov 12 resignation; Mohsin Ali - what to watch Tuesday: Vera Rubin shipments, interim CEO Colette Kress facing questions on the investigation, the reported $105B OpenAI guarantee, and a split Street with HSBC at $170 and Raymond James at $515; Smart Money Bro - bigger than Jensen Huang: why he's still buying Nvidia stock.

item.title: AI Stocks Daily — Nov 14, 2026
item.description: AI bubble: Finance Stack - nearly one in five Korean adults own Samsung, the market has lost nearly half its value, and AI is now a fifth to a third of US growth with the Mag 7 a third of the S&P; Finance Stack - the other side: hyperscalers can afford their debts, the IMF's AI crash scenario is a 2000-size problem not 2008, but SoftBank and Thiel sold all their Nvidia and Burry is short; TheOneLanceB - the correction is hot but not irrationally exuberant, and the Anthropic IPO needs a mildly more cautious stance. Watchlist: Market Signal - a sea of red, $560B wiped off the board, Nvidia down $600B in its worst week on record at about $162; The Creative Investor - the Jensen-comeback rumor, the year-end rally case with Nvidia earnings Tuesday and the Anthropic IPO Monday, and AI-lab valuations that will never justify themselves; Dividend Talks - Broadcom is number one as hyperscalers build their own chips, with a $516 DCF, and the full ranking wrap-up: TSM and Lam S-tier, Micron, SK Hynix and SanDisk opportunity names, Nvidia a measured accumulation.

item.title: AI Stocks Daily — Nov 12, 2026
item.description: AI bubble: Ed Zitron - Nvidia was the bank of AI, and with Huang gone the circular financing that propped up the ecosystem is over (The Tech Report); Paul's Hardware - is the bubble bursting? Trust no one selling a certain answer, and if AI hits a wall, data-center demand falls off hard; TheTechnicalTraders - Nvidia down 11% today, 36% from the highs, and Anthropic's ~$90B IPO looks like a feeding frenzy. Supply/demand: Innovation Uncovered - hyperscalers spent ~$200B on capex in Q3, Meta's free cash flow went negative and buybacks hit the lowest since 2017, so the buildout is now debt-funded; Nick Saraev - OpenAI runs ~100% on Nvidia while Anthropic is only ~33% and is building custom silicon, shifting the compute balance; NBC DFW - Georgia's data centers will double state power demand in five years, and the fight is over who pays for the grid. Watchlist: CBS - the timeline of Huang's resignation, from the affair admissions to the board's move; Schwab/Jablonski - were investors buying Nvidia or Jensen Huang? Demand for compute is intact and a lot of AI stocks are on sale; Schwab/Hanks - the facts: $5.7T to $4.2T market cap, Ives' $225 target without Huang, AMD +23% and Broadcom +17% this week; Tom Lee on CNBC - watch talent retention, the thing that would tell you if Nvidia is weathering this.
